topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Carbon's interactive Mockup Atlas implements Strand v0.2 inline CSS token palettes across three live-switchable WCAG AA themes (cockpit-light, cockpit-dark, high-contrast) plus Rendered/Both/ASCII wireframe inspection modes, zero external fonts or scripts.
why: Demonstrates WCAG AA contrast compliance across all three built-in themes and 18 scenes.

statement: Spreadsheets win because a spatial grid makes state visible and reactive without authoring an app first, but fail when models outgrow an undifferentiated grid where constants masquerade as formulas and silent range truncations look calm.
why: Frames the core UX problem DNA Calc must solve.

statement: 'Excel under the hood, modern on the surface' means separating the calculation substrate from the projection lens without ever separating them in truth: Excel-identical evaluation and plain .xlsx/.xlsm persistence paired with a flight-deck instrument bench projecting one live workbook into five views plus Formula Explorer.
why: Establishes the unified projection architecture.

statement: Rejects the 'clean SaaS spreadsheet' approach with oversized padding and simplified formula dialects because high-speed analysts need density and real workbooks break under non-Excel dialects.
why: Protects power-user velocity and workbook compatibility.

statement: Rejects cloning Excel's multi-tabbed Ribbon because a 280 px icon warehouse buries model diagnostics and starves vertical workspace.
why: Justifies a compact 30 px command strip instead of a Ribbon.

statement: Quality priority order when qualities conflict: Honesty > Familiarity of hands > Clarity of structure > Density of chrome.
why: Provides an explicit tie-breaking hierarchy.

statement: Honesty is absolute: views and Formula Lens may group, fold, label or format formulas, but must never silently drop rows, hide errors inside collapsed blocks, invent non-Excel evaluation rules, or present heuristic inference as certainty.

Familiarity belongs in the hands rather than legacy visual clutter: Classic preserves every Excel veteran keyboard and mouse reflex (F2, F4, F9, Ctrl+Enter, Alt chords, fill-handle double-click) on the first try.

Clarity comes from structural provenance rather than decoration: consistent cues for constants, formulas, external/volatile feeds, fresh recalculations and errors let users spot hardcoded overrides in 200 ms without opening an audit dialog.

Density is modal by task: Working density provides 22 px tabular grid rows and zero wasted gutters where hands edit, while Reading density (Source Serif 4, ~68 ch measure, generous leading) governs Notebook and App consumption.
All workbook views share one calm petrol-800 (#193F49) flight-deck shell wrapping a daylight paper stage (#FFFFFF/#EDF1F2 in cockpit-light, #1A262B in cockpit-dark).

The Mast (top, 34 px) holds the Strand profile badge (twin teal+petrol for workbooks; dot-long cyan+petrol for standalone Formula Explorer), title, non-blocking quarantine pills, 5-view switcher (Ctrl+1..Ctrl+5), Formula Lens toggle (Alt+L), Formula Explorer (Ctrl+Shift+E), Command Palette (Ctrl+K), and Agent Change-Set badge.
The Bridge (30 px, collapsible in App) holds the Unified Address & Target Box, expandable live Formula Bar (Recursive Mono, multi-line LET), and contextual strip tools.
The Stage (14 px top corners) renders the active view per sheet (or workbook-wide in Model Map/Inspector) with bottom-left sheet tabs carrying per-sheet preferred-view micro-glyphs.

The Instrument Strip (bottom, 26 px) is the sole home for persistent telemetry: calculation mode & Director, recalc progress/duration, workbook error count with root count, selection aggregates, and semantic zoom.

why: Enables pairing up to four formula references accessibly without rainbow fills or stealing error red.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Strand refinement 4 (Themes vs Skins): locks Theme (palettes and WCAG AA contrast pairs) to Strand's unit-tested tokens while letting declarative Skins customise layout, panel composition, App cards, density, keymaps and commands without allowing CSS that breaks WCAG AA or repurposes red/amber/signal.
why: Reconciles Strand's three-theme discipline with declarative skin authoring.

statement: Strand refinement 5 (Standalone Formula Explorer badge): binds Strand's dot-long base-pair mark (teal-400 dot + petrol-800 bar) to standalone DNA Calc - Formula Explorer so a workbookless scratchpad is visually distinct from file-backed workbooks (twin mark).

Principle 1 (Backing-Sheet Primacy Rule): any non-grid gesture that cannot express a deterministic, reversible Excel workbook mutation (plus optional customXml metadata) is refused or scoped as view-only annotation (e.g., dragging a map wire rewrites the AST; deleting an App card removes only the layout card).

Principle 2 (Never Summarize Away an Anomaly): collapsing identical formula runs or grouping sheets must always bubble interior errors, hardcoded formula overrides, and broken links onto the parent badge at every zoom level.

Principle 3 (Preview Seam Before Commitment): any high-blast-radius action (25k-row fill, agent hunk, block rewire, F9 sub-eval, iterative tick) displays target scope and reversible preview before committing, and Esc always restores exact prior state.

Principle 4 (One Selection, Five Projections): switching views changes projection rather than place, resolving the selected target in the destination view and pulsing Strand's 150 ms amber continuity halo.

Principle 5 (Quarantine Without Hostage-Taking): untrusted macros, missing external links and heavy recalc queues open immediately in safe cached state behind clear Mast quarantine pills instead of blocking modal startup dialogs.

Cold start (≤65 ms) opens a calm Start Stage on mist paper with no tour popups or account wall, offering Open Workbook (Ctrl+O / drag-and-drop), New Blank Workbook (Ctrl+N), Open Formula Explorer (Ctrl+Shift+E), and a 4-line Excel Power-User Note.

First open of Inherited.xlsm (M-01): snaps petrol shell at 55 ms and paints cached values of active sheet at 190 ms while streaming background dependency indexing (Strip 74% -> 100% at 1,180 ms); replaces Excel's blocking dialogs with a keyboard-reachable Quarantine Bar (Alt+Q: Macros Blocked Module1, 2 Missing Links Held at cached values) and auto-Triage Strip linking to Inspector; Bridge shows inline upstream root-error cell under the Formula Bar; Sheet Drawer [≡ 40 Sheets] reveals sheet formula counts and [+9 Hidden] including VeryHidden; polite screen-reader announcement summarizes file state.

evidence: M-01; Inherited.xlsm (40 sheets, 304,812 fmls, 417 errors / 3 roots)

All five views share the One Shell, honour Formula Lens (Alt+L), and switch in <100 ms via Ctrl+1..Ctrl+5 or Ctrl+K; touch and pen are deferred for v1 with explicit hook points noted per view.

statement: R-31 (Declarative Skin Safety): Skins travelling inside `.xlsx` `customXml` shall contain declarative data only (zero executable scripts), pass automated WCAG AA contrast checks, and never override error/focus/external signal tokens or security banners.

C-1 (Immediate Cached Snapshot on Open): Open a workbook and immediately read sheet names, visibility states (`Visible`, `Hidden`, `VeryHidden`), grid dimensions, formatting, and last-saved cached cell values before full dependency indexing or recalculation completes.

C-2 (Security & External Inventory Up Front): Know on open whether the file contains VBA/macro modules, external workbook links (and whether their targets are reachable), `RTD` topics, or add-in UDF calls, and hold macros/broken links inactive until instructed.

C-3 (Cell, Name, and Block Precedents & Dependents): Query direct and transitive precedents and dependents for any cell, range, or defined name—including dynamic references (`INDEX`, `XLOOKUP`, `FILTER`, `OFFSET`, `INDIRECT`) resolved from the latest calculation—both at individual cell granularity and summarised by Defined Name, block, and sheet (preserving name-to-name edges rather than dropping names down to raw cells).

C-4 (Calculation Delta & Order Notification): Be told after every recalculation which cells and defined names changed value, what their previous and new values are, which external/`RTD` event or user edit triggered the pass, and a topological dependency ordering among changed items, plus elapsed time per sheet/stage.

C-5 (Root-Error Attribution): Given all cells currently holding `#` error values, know which cells are root origins (producing an error from non-error inputs) versus downstream propagations, along with the shortest error path from root to any dependent cell.

C-6 (R1C1 Formula Equivalence & Anomaly Detection): Group contiguous runs of cells that share an identical relative (R1C1) formula structure into single blocks, and be told of interior anomalies—such as a literal constant overriding one cell inside a formula run, or a range reference (`Orders!$I$2:$I$22000`) that covers most but not all rows of an Excel Table (`Orders`).

C-7 (Parsed Syntax Tree & Lossless Name Rewriting): Obtain the syntax tree of any formula (with character spans for every reference, literal, operator, and function call) and rewrite references bidirectionally between raw Excel syntax and scoped/shortened defined names without touching strings, comments, or function identifiers.

C-8 (Side-Effect-Free Sub-Expression & Sandbox Evaluation): Evaluate any selected sub-expression (`F9` in Formula Bar), complete scratchpad `LET`/`LAMBDA` expression, or temporary "what-if" input override (for Formula Explorer and Boundary Probes) and get back its exact value, data type, spill dimensions, number-formatted string, and conditional-formatting rule match—without mutating or dirtying the live workbook.

C-9 (Workbookless Standalone Engine Mode): Start the formula parser, 500+ built-in Excel functions, number formatter, conditional-format evaluator, and add-in UDF host with no workbook loaded at all (`DNA Calc - Formula Explorer`).

C-10 (Excel Calculation Mode & Iterative Parameters): Read and set workbook calculation mode (`Automatic`, `Automatic Except Data Tables`, `Manual`), `Iterative Calculation` enablement, `Maximum Iterations`, and `Maximum Change`, and trigger single recalculation steps (`F9` / `Shift+F9` / full rebuild) on demand.

C-11 (Dirty / Stale State Visibility): Know under `Manual` calculation mode (or mid-stream during large async recalculations) which cells and blocks are currently dirty/stale relative to upstream edits.
C-12 (Dynamic Spill Boundaries & Blockers): Know for every dynamic-array anchor cell its current spilled rectangle (`B14:E21`), or—if `#SPILL!` occurs—the exact cells blocking the spill.

C-13 (Native Table, Pivot, Data-Table & Control Metadata): Read and update Excel `ListObject` tables (headers, column names, total rows), `PivotTable` source ranges/axes/cached values, What-If `{=TABLE(row, col)}` definitions, charts, and Form Control bindings (`ScrollBar` min/max/step/linked cell).

C-14 (Custom XML View Part Round-Trip): Read and write arbitrary UTF-8 XML/JSON blobs in a dedicated custom part of `.xlsx` / `.xlsm` files that desktop Excel ignores and preserves intact across edits and saves.

C-15 (Structural Fingerprint Reconciliation): Compute lightweight label/formula fingerprints for ranges referenced by custom view settings so that if rows or columns were inserted in desktop Excel while DNA Calc was closed, moved blocks can be located on re-open.

C-16 (Copy-on-Write Staged Change-Sets): Apply a batch of proposed edits (from an AI agent or refactor preview) onto an isolated fork of the workbook, read the resulting diffs across all affected cells and summary KPIs, and selectively commit chosen subsets or discard with zero residual state.

C-17 (Atomic & Compound Undo/Redo Checkpoints): Group multi-cell fills, agent hunks, or VBA macro runs into named, reversible checkpoints that restore exact values, formulas, formatting, and calculation state in `O(changed cells)` time.

C-18 (Non-Locking Add-in UDF Host & Metadata): Load and unload `.xll` / add-in packages without locking their files on disk, enumerate exported function names, argument descriptions, return types, thread-safety, and volatility flags, and store portable `_xll.` prefixes + cached results in `.xlsx`.

C-19 (Non-Blocking Cancellation & Viewport Priority): Keep viewport reads, edits, and `Esc` cancellation responsive while indexing or recalculating 300,000+ formulas in the background, prioritizing cells visible on screen or displayed in the Strip.

C-20 (Fast Aggregate & Criteria Mismatch Queries): Compute Strip aggregates (`Sum`, `Avg`, `Count`, `Min`, `Max`) over multi-thousand-cell selections instantaneously, and identify near-miss rows in a table column (e.g., `"West "` with trailing whitespace or text-stored numbers `"37000"`) when auditing `SUMIFS`/`XLOOKUP` discrepancies.

C-21 (Excel PageSetup & Print Geometry): Read and write Excel `PageSetup` settings (`PrintArea`, `PrintTitles`, manual/automatic page breaks, orientation, scaling) and query exact row/column pagination boundaries for `Classic` print parity.
C-22 (Goal Seek Single-Input Solver): Solve for a single numeric input cell needed to make a formula cell hit a target number (powering App View's safe `[Solve Principal for $2,400/mo…]` action).
